topics.label: Citizenship through Adoption
topics.metaDescription: How an adopted child of a Canadian citizen can obtain direct citizenship — eligibility, and how this differs from PR sponsorship.
topics.lead: Children adopted by a Canadian citizen parent may be eligible for direct Canadian citizenship, rather than needing to first obtain permanent residence through family sponsorship — a distinction that depends on the adopting parent's status and the adoption's specific circumstances.
headings: Citizenship vs. PR Sponsorship for Adopted Children

topics.label: PR through Adoption
topics.metaDescription: Permanent residence pathway for children adopted by a Canadian permanent resident — sponsorship process and requirements.
topics.lead: When the adopting parent is a Canadian permanent resident (rather than a citizen), the adopted child's route to Canada generally runs through family class sponsorship for permanent residence, rather than a direct citizenship grant.
headings: After the Child Becomes a Permanent Resident

topics.label: Proof of Adoption Record
topics.seoTitle: Proof of Adoption Record Canada 2026 | CMG
topics.metaDescription: What documentation is needed to prove a legal adoption for Canadian immigration or citizenship purposes.
topics.lead: Both the citizenship-through-adoption and PR-through-adoption routes depend on establishing a clear, legally recognized adoption record — the specific documents required can vary significantly depending on the country where the adoption took place.

topics.label: Criminal Inadmissibility (overview)
topics.seoTitle: Criminal Inadmissibility Canada 2026: TRP & Rehabilitation | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Criminal inadmissibility to Canada explained: Temporary Resident Permits, Criminal Rehabilitation, and Deemed Rehabilitation eligibility timelines.
topics.lead: A criminal record — even one from decades ago, or for an offence considered minor in another country — can make a person inadmissible to Canada. Several routes exist to overcome inadmissibility depending on the offence, how much time has passed, and the purpose of travel.

topics.label: Criminal Rehabilitation
topics.metaDescription: Permanently resolve criminal inadmissibility to Canada. Eligibility timeline, equivalency assessment, and application process explained.
topics.lead: Criminal Rehabilitation is a formal application that permanently resolves inadmissibility caused by a past criminal conviction, once enough time has passed since the sentence was completed — distinct from a Temporary Resident Permit, which only authorizes a single trip or period.

topics.label: Temporary Resident Permit (TRP)
topics.metaDescription: TRP applications for travellers who are otherwise inadmissible to Canada — when case-by-case entry can still be authorized.
topics.lead: A Temporary Resident Permit allows entry to Canada despite an existing inadmissibility, issued case by case when the need to travel is found to outweigh the risk associated with the inadmissibility — useful for time-sensitive travel while a permanent solution like Criminal Rehabilitation is still pending or not yet available.

topics.label: Record Suspension / Pardon
topics.metaDescription: How a Canadian record suspension (pardon) affects immigration inadmissibility, and how it differs from foreign rehabilitation routes.
topics.lead: A Canadian record suspension — commonly still called a pardon — addresses a Canadian criminal conviction specifically, generally sealing it from most background checks. Its immigration impact differs from Criminal Rehabilitation, which addresses foreign convictions.
headings: Limits of a Pardon or Record Suspension
Canadian Record Suspension vs. Immigration Remedies

topics.label: Deemed Rehabilitation
topics.metaDescription: How older, less serious foreign convictions can be automatically resolved without a formal application — eligibility explained.
topics.lead: Deemed Rehabilitation can automatically resolve inadmissibility for older, less serious foreign convictions once enough time has passed — without requiring a formal Criminal Rehabilitation application, provided the offence and timeline meet the applicable criteria.
